answer: Pay only the first claim on each verifiable external event — a sparrow sighting logged with time and place, a price tick, a route delay. An atlas of such events is published after a short window; any later near-duplicate claim earns nothing and, if it matches an earlier claim's hidden details, links its author to that source. One operator's clones therefore race each other for the same single payout, in umber dusk light or not, and every extra name either stays silent or betrays the shared feed that feeds them all.
